parameters.content:
## Project Showcase Publisher

Publishes Luna's project case Docs (Google Drive: Case案例 → Upload) as posts in the Shopify blog **Project Showcase** (marblebee.com/blogs/project-showcase), translated to English, using the `showcase` theme templates.

**One case per run.** Each run picks the lowest case number (CA###, read from the Doc name) that has no post yet, so a case is never posted twice. A case counts as done when a post in the blog has its tag (e.g. `CA009`), draft or published. Run it once per case, or activate it and the hourly trigger works through new Docs on its own.

**Flow:** list Docs → skip done cases → read the Doc's structure from the Google Docs API (no size limit; Drive's export refuses Docs over 10 MB) → turn it into tagged text with [[IMG_n]] photo placeholders → GPT-4.1 (OpenAI node) translates to English and rebuilds clean HTML (same order, same photo positions) → photos are copied from the Doc into Shopify Files → placeholders become Shopify CDN images (each photo full width, same order and position as in the Doc; bold text kept) → post created with template `showcase`, tag = case number, featured image = first photo.

**Set Config → publish**: `false` creates hidden drafts to review in Shopify admin; set `true` to publish directly.

**If a run fails** nothing is posted (the post is created last), so fix the cause and run again. Photos are never uploaded twice: an update keeps every photo that is unchanged in the Doc (any age; the Doc-image-id → URL map is stored on the post as metafield showcase.image_map, so admin edits can't lose it), and a re-run after a failure reuses what that run already uploaded (last 3 days). When nothing needs uploading the 15 s wait is skipped.

**Limits:** the existing-posts check reads the newest 250 posts of the blog; add pagination before the blog passes 250 cases.

**Nodes:** Google Drive and OpenAI use n8n's own nodes. Shopify calls are HTTP Request nodes because n8n's Shopify node has no blog-post or Files operations. "Get Doc" is an HTTP Request to the Google Docs API so it can reuse the existing Google Drive login (the Google Docs node only accepts its own credential type).

**Update a posted case:** set Set Config → `updateCase` to its number (e.g. `CA002`), run once, then clear it. The case is re-read from its Doc and the existing post is overwritten (same URL, visibility unchanged).

**Log:** every created/updated case is written to the Google Sheet "Project Showcase Log" → tab `Cases` (one row per case, matched on Case No; First Published comes from Shopify, Last Updated is the run time).

', $aid: ID!' : '') + ') { files(first: 250, sortKey: CREATED_AT, reverse: true, query: $q) { nodes { id alt fileStatus } }' + (aid ? ' article(id: $aid) { body metafield(namespace: "showcase", key: "image_map") { value } }' : '') + ' }'; const v = { q: "media_type:IMAGE AND created_at:>'" + $now.minus({ days: 3 }).toISO() + "'" }; if (aid) v.aid = 'gid://shopify/Article/' + aid; return JSON.stringify({ query: q, variables: v }); })() }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ query: 'mutation fileCreate($files: [FileCreateInput!]!) { fileCreate(files: $files) { files { id alt fileStatus } userErrors { field message } } }', variables: { files: $('Skip Already Uploaded').first().json.toUpload.map(i => ({ alt: $('Parse Doc').first().json.caseNo + ' - Image ' + i.n, contentType: 'IMAGE', originalSource: i.src })) } }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ query: 'query files($ids: [ID!]!) { nodes(ids: $ids) { ... on MediaImage { id alt fileStatus fileErrors { message } image { url } } } }', variables: { ids: $('Skip Already Uploaded').first().json.reuseIds.concat($('Upload Images to Shopify').isExecuted ? ((($('Upload Images to Shopify').first().json.data || {}).fileCreate || { files: [] }).files.map(f => f.id)) : []) } }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ query: 'mutation set($m: [MetafieldsSetInput!]!) { metafieldsSet(metafields: $m) { metafields { id } userErrors { field message } } }', variables: { m: [{ ownerId: 'gid://shopify/Article/' + $json.article.id, namespace: 'showcase', key: 'image_map', type: 'json', value: JSON.stringify($('Build Article').first().json.imageMap) }] } }) }}
